items.title: In a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring the number of minimal primes is bounded by the length of the quotient by an element avoiding them
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension 1, an element x in m not contained in any minimal prime of R, and the number t of minimal primes, and asserts t <= length_R(R/xR) (source lines 38015-38021). The proof first reduces to the reduced case: putting R' = R/sqrt(0), the ring R' has the same number t of minimal primes and its quotient R'/xR' is a surjective image of R/xR, hence has smaller length (proof lines 38024-38030). For reduced R the proof uses the exact sequence 0 -> R -> prod_i R/p_i -> Q -> 0, computes that Q localized at any p_j vanishes, so that the support of Q is the single prime m, which makes Q of finite length and killed by a power x^n of x (proof lines 38033-38056). The substantive computation is then the snake lemma applied to the displayed square of multiplication-by-x^n maps: because x is not in any p_i, multiplication by x^n is injective on R and on M, and the snake sequence gives 0 -> Q -> R/x^nR -> M/x^nM -> Q -> 0, whence length_R(R/x^nR) = length_R(M/x^nM) for large n (proof lines 38057-38072). Splitting M as the product of the R_i = R/p_i and applying the one-dimensional polynomial-length lemma with x a nonzerodivisor gives n length_R(R/xR) = sum_i n length_{R_i}(R_i/xR_i), and since each term on the right is at least 1 the bound t <= length_R(R/xR) follows (proof lines 38073-38082). The non-routine steps are the support computation for Q and the snake-lemma length identity.
